Definition: neuter of a presumed derivative of G696; silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel):--money, (piece of) silver (piece).
BiblicalUsage: The word is silver as money, cash, the price of things. Peter says silver and gold have I none, but what I have I give thee; Simon is told his money will perish with him for thinking God's gift can be bought; Judas covenants for thirty pieces of silver; and Peter says we were not redeemed with corruptible things like silver and gold.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that silver is the Bible's measure of what money can and cannot do. It buys a betrayal, it cannot buy the gift of God, and it cannot redeem a soul, which is why the price of our redemption had to be something else entirely.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
